question: Which of the following gases, when cooled and compressed, can change from a gas to a supercritical fluid state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide (CO₂)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon dioxide (CO₂)** can transition to a supercritical fluid state when cooled and compressed beyond its critical temperature and pressure.
 
• A supercritical fluid is a state of matter where distinct liquid and gas phases do not exist.
 
• Supercritical CO2 is commonly used in various industrial applications, including supercritical fluid extraction and as a solvent in chemical processes.
 
• The critical temperature and pressure for **CO₂ are 31.1°C and 73.8 atm**, respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supercritical fluids** have properties of both liquids and gases, making them versatile in various scientific and industrial processes.
 
• The use of supercritical CO₂ is favored for its** non-toxic, non-flammable nature** and its ability to act as a solvent without the need for hazardous chemicals.
 
• Other gases can also become supercritical fluids under the right conditions, but CO₂ is one of the most commonly utilized due to its relatively low critical temperature and pressure.
 
• Understanding the behavior of supercritical fluids is important in fields such as materials science, chemistry, and engineering.
